title: 09. Deep Learning: Activation Functions
summary: Activation functions are the non-linear transformations that give neural networks their power. Without them, even deep networks would collapse into simple linear models.

title: 09. Deep Learning: Forward & Backward Propagation
summary: Backpropagation is the algorithm that makes deep learning possible. It efficiently computes gradients for all parameters in a neural network using the chain rule of calculus.

title: 09. Deep Learning: Deep Learning Loss Functions
summary: Loss functions (or cost functions) measure how well your model's predictions match the true labels. They are the optimization objective that guides learning through backpropagation.

title: 09. Deep Learning: Weight Initialization
summary: Weight initialization is one of the most critical yet often overlooked aspects of training neural networks.

title: 09. Deep Learning: Gradient Issues (Vanishing & Exploding Gradients)
summary: Gradient problems are the main obstacles to training deep neural networks. They occur when gradients become extremely small (vanishing) or extremely large (exploding) as they propagate backward through layers, making training impossible.

title: 09. Deep Learning: Batch Normalization
summary: Batch Normalization (BatchNorm) is one of the most impactful innovations in deep learning.

title: 09. Deep Learning: Dropout & Regularization in Deep Learning
summary: Regularization prevents overfitting - when a model learns training data too well but fails to generalize to new data. In deep learning with millions of parameters, overfitting is a constant threat.

title: 09. Deep Learning: Gradient Descent Variants
summary: Gradient Descent is the fundamental optimization algorithm for training neural networks. However, the basic version has limitations.

title: 09. Deep Learning: Advanced Optimizers
summary: Beyond basic gradient descent, advanced optimizers use momentum, adaptive learning rates, and other techniques to dramatically improve training speed and stability. These algorithms are the workhorses of modern deep learning.

title: 09. Deep Learning: Learning Rate Strategies
summary: The learning rate is the most important hyperparameter in deep learning. Too large → training diverges.

title: 09. Deep Learning: Training Stability
summary: Training instability can derail your deep learning project. Exploding gradients, NaN losses, and diverging training are common nightmares.

title: 09. Deep Learning: Mixed Precision Training
summary: Mixed precision training uses both FP16 (half precision) and FP32 (single precision) to train models 2x faster with ~50% less memory, while maintaining accuracy. This is now standard practice in modern deep learning.

title: 09. Deep Learning: Gradient Accumulation
summary: Gradient accumulation allows training with large effective batch sizes without requiring massive GPU memory. It's essential for training large models and achieving stable optimization when hardware is limited.

title: 09. Deep Learning: Training Checkpointing
summary: Training checkpointing is essential for saving and resuming long training runs. It prevents data loss from crashes, enables experimentation, and allows continued training across sessions.

title: 09. Deep Learning: Hyperparameter Tuning for Deep Learning
summary: Hyperparameter tuning is the process of finding the best configuration for your model. Unlike model parameters (learned during training), hyperparameters are set before training begins.

title: 09. Deep Learning: Convolution Operations
summary: Convolution is the fundamental operation in CNNs that enables spatial feature detection. Unlike fully connected layers, convolutions preserve spatial relationships and are translation-invariant.

title: 09. Deep Learning: Pooling Layers
summary: Pooling layers downsample feature maps, reducing spatial dimensions while retaining important features. They provide translation invariance and reduce computation.
